The controller is very intuitive and easy to use as well, and was definitely a nice upgrade for me from my previous grill. 

This grill gets up to temperature very quickly. Even on a couple of sub-freezing days, I was able to set it to maximum temperature without any issues. 

So far I have made ribs, nachos, and brisket on this new grill and so far I am so glad that I went with this model. Definitely recommended!

title: Best Grill Evah!
text:
I have been looking for a grill for a while and bit the bullet with my new Traeger. The first thing I ever cooked was a whole chicken, no way I could do that on my old Aussie grill! Food tastes great and its so great to be able to just leave it alone and not tend to it every 5 minutes or so.

Couple of things to fix to make it better, fix the app. If you let your phone go to sleep sometimes it wakes up but mostly you have to shut down the app and relaunch it to see the current readings.

Pellet sensor, not sure why you cant have a pellets low warning on the above mentioned app?

Pellet hatch, great idea for cleaning out or changing pellets but... Why not put a shoot (Or a shoot with a hook for the bucket even better) on the hatch? I guess there is a technique but so far I have not managed to capture all the pellets and some inevitably end up on the floor.

Stupid minor things yeah but would be an improvement!

title: Easy to use!
text:
I've been grilling with a gas grill for over 20 years and recently switched to the Traeger Pro 780 Pellet Grill - and I have no intention of ever going back to gas. My Traeger is so simple to use, easy to clean, and produces consistently amazing results every time whether it's burgers, ribs, chicken, or baked goods. 

I love the new WiFire feature that lets me control the grill temperaturate, kick it into Keep Warm mode or monitor cooking progress when using the temp probe. It really doesn't get an easier, or better, than cooking with on a Traeger.

title: Pro 780 Good Purchase
text:
I’ll break Thai review into pro’s and Con’s

Pro
-Really well constructed and easy assemble and use
-Setting temperature or receive temp is a snap
- App is handy with FireWire to monitor cooking. Set up was really easy as well. My IPhone stays connected all the way to the street while smoker is in back yard
-Really like the integrated meat thermometer 

Con
-Temperature varies too much spiking or dropping up to 10 degrees at a time
-Searing is good not great and smoking at low temp (175) not getting same smoke flavor as I do from my Komodo Joe. So searing and smoking both are average. 
-Some felt along the door would have helped insulate the smoker better.

title: Great for beginners or pro grillers
text:
I'm super new to pellet grills and was excited to get this version. Set up was super simple and seasoning was straight forward. We could hardly wait to fire this up and get cooking. We've used it about a dozen times. Here are a few pros and cons we've found: 

Pros: 
Heats quickly and gets back to temp fast when you have to open the lid
Connects to your phone for easy controls (my husbands favorite feature)
Keeps track of the internal temp of your food with a probe (also connects to your phone)
Easy to clean

Cons:
We honestly can't think of any. 

With the summer heat making it less appealing to turn on our oven, we find ourselves using this more and more. A few of our favorite recipes so far: meatloaf, brats philly style, lasagna, and fajitas. All super yummy and cooked perfect. Already talked a few friends into purchasing their own after backyard barbecues.

title: Buyer Beware.
text:
Let me say this first, the food has been great off this grill. The grill itself was easy to assemble and almost operated as it should.

Now for the reason behind the 1star. The temperatures that the digital read out shows are way off! At lower temps (180) it was off by 20-50 degrees. And at higher temps (275) it was between 50-100 degrees off! Not a windy day, sunny, and low 90’s outside. I used two different oven thermometers and a separate digital probe and the grill was definitely off. 

I had so many issues with customer service during the ordering process that I have not called them yet about this problem. I’m actually dreading it. For $1,000 this holiday be an issue but as I’ve since found out it is an issue and we’ll complained about amongst Traeger groups on Reddit and other services. 

I would’ve returned this grill but of course the fine print states it must be in its original packaging and you are responsible for the return shipping. It was such a masterful artwork of packaging that no one could get it back together.

You have to exit and close the app and relaunch the app.  My suggestion is to always exit and close the app when viewing and adjusting settings on your smoker via phone app.  Lastly the notification for the probe temp being reach can be delayed. title: The flavor gods have smiled down on this grill!
text: Ok, so the only reason you should need to get a pellet grill is the flavor. If you're still using another type of grill, you're basically wasting your meat. Stop it. The flavor of everything we've cooked on this bad boy is on a different level. Now the reasons you should get a Traeger, specifically this newer line is the speed and the ease of use. This thing goes from ambient temps to 450 in about 6 or 7 minutes. Wow, from what I understand that has a lot to do with the newer D2 motor, I expected to have to wait forever for the grill to warm up, and have been pleasantly surprised that wasn't the case. The WiFIRE is the next reason you should get this grill, or another grill that includes that feature. Being able to check the temperatures of both the grill and the probe, as well as make adjustments from your phone is truly a game changer. You can even load recipes from the Traeger app to the grill and it will change the temps as needed for you! What a world. The quality of this thing is incredible, built like a tank, and the attention to detail paid creates a high level fit and finish that you wouldn't expect to see on a "grill". If you're in the market, good news, your search is over.

title: Pellet problem, not BBQ problem
text: I bought a Traeger Pro at Costco which came with pellets and it worked great for 6 months. Bought another bag of pellets at Costco and the pellets are 2 inches long, glossy, and hard as rocks. Now my BBQ will 'auto shut-off' for low temp and 'auto shut-off' for high temp, and just having all sorts of temperature fluctuations. Since the BBQ worked great on the other pellets, I finally figured out it was the pellets. The problem I found was the new pellets are too long, and the auger can't break them up and jambing, causing low temp. When it finally surges and spits a ton of pellets into the 'firepot', it gets too hot. I contacted Traeger, and was told the pellets they sell on their website "don't do this". I bought Trager branded pellets from Costco so how was I to know? The grill gets 5 stars, C.S. gets 1 star making 3 stars. Here is the fix: I finally put some pellets in a bucket and smashed them with a sledge hammer. The grill works great now. Just cooked a tri-tip for 6 hours on smoke, no problem. NOW I just need to smash 33 pounds for pellets from Costco. Not thrilled.

title: Phenomenal Grill, Extremely Well Constructed!
text: I absolutely love this grill!  I ordered it directly from TraegerGrills.com.  I was worried about damage in shipment, but it was packed so well that there was it arrived in pristine condition.  I then unpacked it and found several surprises -- more on that later.  I began putting it together and the instructions, parts, and hardware made it seamless.  They even include the screwdriver, crescent wrench and allen wrench you will need.  I had it assembled in no time.  I do highly recommend you have another person nearby for some parts of assembly, such as flipping it over to attach the legs, as you'll have a higher risk of  damaging your grill if you do it by yourself.  Its very sturdy and heavy.  Once assembled, the instructions on how to start it up were simple and very easy to follow.  I did run into one small issue with connecting the WiFi portion, and I was worried that I'd be dead in the water since this was 4p on a Saturday, but I saw their support line was open 365 days per year from morning until evening.  I called and I was the 6th person in the queue.  It provided me the option to stay on the line or to keep my place in line and have support call me back. I elected for the latter.  In 2 minutes they called my phone, were very polite, well-spoken and wonderfully helpful.  They helped me solve the issue in less than a minute by asking me a couple of quick questions to assess where in the process I was running into the issue.  Now I was ready to grill!  I first seasoned it following the instructions.   Note: this takes about an hour, so plan on that, but it needs to be done.  Once that was complete, I let the grill cool down all the way because I wanted to see how long it would take to go from ambient temp up to 450 -- it was 23F degrees outside at the time.  To my surprise, it was lightening fast, and even better, I could see the temp increasing real-time from inside my house right on my app.    I then backed it off to the temp I wanted to cook at -- I had two big, juicy steaks to cook.  It cooked them perfectly!  I had two college buddies in town visiting this weekend and they both said the steak was phenomenal with perfect wood-fired flavor.  I used the Signature Blend of Traeger pellets.  My buddies raved about the taste even the next day.  I love this grill and am stoked with my purchase.  Now on to the nice surprises.  I have 3 young children (5, 8 and 11 yrs old).  When I opened the box after it was delivered, I could see printing on the inside of the box.  Well, if you turn the cardboard box inside out after unpacking it, it turns into a playhouse with the printing being a design that looks like a rustic cabin, complete with a window, a door, shakes roof, and an image of the grill in the front of the cabin.   I set it up in the kids' playroom and they had a blast all weekend acting like they were camping "at the cabin."  What kid doesn't love a huge cardboard box to play in? And the printing on it made so much better for imaginary play.  The second nice surprise is the assembly instructions come with suggested amount of your "favorite bottled beverage" to consume with each major step.   Every great assembly project needs the operator to be appropriately well-oiled with assembly juice, right?  I highly recommend this grill.

text:
I bought this grill two months ago, extremely excited about my first Traeger, and I've used it about a dozen times. My thoughts:

The good:
-Food tastes pretty good (food also tastes good on a $100 charcoal grill)
-Very difficult to overcook anything 

The bad:
-Display screen is already failing (see photo, bottom left corner of screen)
-Meat temperature probe broke after 1 use (bad probe error sign whenever I plug it in)
-Despite what Traeger advertises, it does not sear meat. If I crank it up to the max setting, 450, I can get weak grill marks on meat at best
-Still haven't found a true smoke setting, even under 200 degrees it doesn't get smoky enough

Overall, this thing basically functions as an outdoor oven. The only benefit over an oven is that it imparts a woody flavor to the food. If you want to drop Traeger $$$ on an outdoor oven, go for it. If I could do it again I'd stick with a much more affordable and less frustrating charcoal grill.

text: My wife and I love to grill year round, we have have used a number of different grills over the years.  She recently suggested we upgrade to a Traeger from our cheaply made Pit Boss pellet grill.  So the first thing I fixed were country style ribs. As soon as I put them on I had turned the temp to 160, we had leave to run into town.  The trip was longer than we had planned and I figured my ribs would be burnt to a crisp!  This pellet grill is amazing the ribs were done perfect, not dry, not burnt. The old saying you get what you pay for and this is by far well worth it!  I'm looking forward to cooking a turkey and ham on it for Christmas dinner!

title: Good if you want an outdoor oven.
text: I have to say I had high hopes, but am extremely disappointed in the Traeger.   I do have some good things to say about it.  It is really easy to use for starters, which is probably the best thing about it. The WiFire is actually an awesome feature.   As far as cooking, if you want to use it as an oven it is pretty good.  It will do most things that any other oven can do.  However if you have expectations that this is going to be a grill or a smoker, don't buy it.  It sort of does both,  but very poorly.  If you are using it as a grill, the indirect heat just is not enough to get a sear on anything. And as a smoker,  well it will slow cook, but there is no smoke flavor. Like none. The only thing I have been able to get decent smoke flavor on is roasted vegetables.  Outside that there is no detectable smoke flavor on chicken, fish, beef or anything else I have tried on it.   I have had a host of other smokers, from charcoal, to propane, to electric, to straight wood.  all of them were a quarter the price of the traeger and all were far superior.  I had no expectations that it was going to match the wood fired smoker,  but it cant even come close to a cheap electric smoker.

I would say the only downsides is that its pretty tough to get a proper sear on steaks, everything else has turned out really well. the wifire has worked well for me, super nice to change/shut down the temperature remotely.

title: Just get one
text:
I read every review I could find, weighed the pros and cons, went back and forth, sat on the fence, and refused to buy one because “I’m a charcoal guy.” Well after my Weber was broken during a move, I decided to replace it with the Traeger...
I wish I hadn’t waited so long. Everything I cook is delicious and cooked to near perfection. Instead of going out to eat on the weekends, we just try new recipes.
Hopefully others had the same questions I had that I can answer here:
-In 3 months I’ve gone through a total of 3 bags of pellets. I use the grill every single Sunday for food prep for the week. On extended weekends I’ll use it up to 3 times. I smoked a turkey and a brisket on Thanksgiving and only went through about half a bag of pellets in about 12-13 hours of smoke.
-Unless you already have some sort of rolling BBQ cart/stand, just buy the front shelf. I wish I had bought it with the original purchase. I ultimately ended up ordering one.
-So far, I’ve used hickory as the universal go to pellet. My local Home Depot only carries mesquite and hickory so I was limited in my options. I’m starting to order some of the other pellet flavors but I want to make sure I’m going to use them for multiple recipes.
-Use the probe, the “times may vary due to weather conditions” statement is very true.
-Be prepared to plan your meals a few days in advance. The wait times for marination is totally worth it.
-Make a brisket.

Hope this helps someone as indecisive as I was.

title: Love the temperature control.
text:
OK, So I bought the Traeger Pro. I was skeptical to say the least given the hefty price. 
I want to say from the get go that I have never done a brisket in my life. I've done many a slab of ribs and pulled porks but never a brisket since I'm not a big fan of brisket in the first place.
My brisket only weighed about 4 pounds. I only bought it because I have this new grill and due to COVID-19 the local grocery store had nothing else worthy of such a grill. I did my research and cooked the thing with the timer at about 5 hours with the temp probe in the meat. When it reached 195 degrees at right at 5 hours. I pulled it off the grill and let it rest for 45 minutes. I finally cut into it for a taste at the pointed end. It was terrible. Both my wife and I agreed it tasted like liver. I hate liver. I have always hated liver. I was about to throw the whole thing away when I decided to cut into it at it's widest point. It was much juicier and tender there and really not bad. The Traeger coffee rub flavor really came out well. The liver flavor seemed to be a problem with the meat itself and nothing to do with the cook. I once had prime rib at a restaurant that tasted the same way. Never knew why and still don't today. The main thing was I was amazed at the precise temperature control maintained through out the cook. My past experience is with Weber 26 inch kettle grills with either my Smokenator or my Slow & Sear. This was by far superior. I can't wait to do some ribs which is my specialty or a pork butt. I think I'm done with brisket. Never wanted it in the first place. If any one knows why some cuts of meat has a liver flavor, I'd sure like to hear about it.
I also wanted to say, with the drip pan and bucket clean up was a breeze. Pretty much just cleaned the grate. I also liked using the mobile app which was by far better than my Maverick temperature probes. 
I love the grill I can't wait until the market has some better selection of meat to complete my purchase.

Tech wise it’s not the most reliable. My grill has crashed twice while I’ve had it, sometimes it takes an hour to heat up. I’m not reporting it because let’s face it, I’m not moving that thing. Nor is it that deep.. I just want you to be informed about this product and if you are going to make an investment and use your grill every other day then I suggest getting something less expensive. As it is I’m scared to over work my Traeger because I still owe on it. Do I have buyers remorse, no. I knew what I was getting myself into. But if you’re an avid bbq enthusiast and your life revolves around smoking meat and grilling than look elsewhere. But if you’re not worried about spending money and don’t care about how long it lasts and don’t bbq but twice a month than this is your product.

Because there is a fan that circulates the heat, it also circulates a bit of the dust.  It is also recommended to purchase a shop vac to vacuum the dust.  Also, the chimney end of the grill seems to have a hot spot, as well as the edges of the grease ramp.  I noticed my left rack of ribs (chimney side) was cooking quicker than the others.  It could have been the rack of ribs but my gut tells me it's hotter on that end.  The smoke is a bit mild but I can live with that with the ease of use.  Overall, I like the grill, however I find myself charing steaks on my green egg and finishing them on the Traeger.

Solution, replace the control board under warranty. You wouldn't believe how hard it is to actually accomplish this or how many zip ties were employed. Never the less, i got it done and back up and running. Then this past week, while smoking ribs 3,2,1 method near the end of step 2, the temp kept dropping, fan and pellet worm still turning. I set the ribs on my gas grill to keep them steaming and opened the grill. The burn pot was over flowing with pellets and there were about three or four more full pots worth in the bottom. I can't imagine what would happen if it suddenly started working again, but stay turned.
Traeger wanted a video since they were sure on or the other fan or worm were not working. during the call I got disconnected, no call back. Two shutdowns and restarts later I got it working. Finishined. 

Then durning a heat up to burn off the gunk, same thing happened again and when I went to check after about 10-15 minutes to see if I was done, temp is 550 and the grill is on fire. Discovered they don't use high temp paint since there are now several spots where it's blistered.

So now they are replacing the temp probe and heating element under warranty. I'll wait and see what's next.

title: It's a Traeger - Not a Grill
text: I purchased my Pro 575 a few weeks ago and I'm really enjoying it.  The assy was very simple and I only needed help to roll it over onto all four.  TIP - Use some masking tape and securely tape the door and hopper lid so that they don't fly open during assy.  Overall it took about an hour to assemble.  I moved on to the seasoning of the Traeger and it went just as in the manual.  Since then I've smoked some ribeyes and made a blackberry cobbler.  I now have a rack of baby back ribs on low and slow (3-2-1) and the Traeger is performing excellently after 2 hours into the cook.  I love the Traeger app even though I'm still learning how to use features such as the cook now in the recipes.  I've also swapped out the Signature for the Hickory pellets for my ribs.  That was very easy using the trap door.  I also used a wooden spoon to push the remaining pellets out into the bucket.  Then just topped it off with hickory pellets and on my way.  TIP - Purchase an HD Homer bucket and lid to store pellets in and help with swapping pellets.  Overall the cooking process has been very simple and I enjoy being able to check on my Traeger from my couch using the app.  I am looking into a searing plate to help sear steaks.  Even at 450F the sear wasn't quite what I like on my steaks and the sear plate will help with that.  Overall, I do recommend the Pro 575.  It has everything I want without all of the bells and whistles AND WiFire.  Just remember it's a Traeger and not your run of the mill grill.  Do your research to understand what a Traeger is compared to a grill to help with your purchase.  All in all you won't be disappointed in the Traeger.

title: Very disappointing
text:
Very disappointed after having had the Pro 575 for almost six weeks and used 2 - 3 times per week. 
1) The temperatures fluctuate heavily more than 10 degrees Celsius and has resulted in dried out food on every low and slow cook (no it is not due to frequently opening the grill - only as per app recipe steps to spritz). Apparently this is actually a know issue by Traeger yet to be resolved by config.
2) large amounts of ash are produced and leave residue on the food, grates and grill opening (this was from the start and the grill is cleaned after EVERY use)
3) Grill Temperature sensor has already lost it's coating
4) Very little smoke is produced and can hardly be tasted (yes I understand the difference between white and blue smoke and yes this was on low / slow cooking)

The Pro 575 clearly needs the super smoke function and needs better configuration to handle the temperature variations.

title: A lot of medium sized irks eventually add up
text:
Pretty disappointed with my grill…not but a couple of months old and I’ve finally had enough medium issues that I’m pretty upset with the way this has been performing. My reason for choosing Traeger was I thought I was paying more for quality and durability, though I’ve found this is incorrect. I’ll also let it be known I’ve never written a one star review, pretty bummed this has to be my first.

I’d like to think I take care of my stuff, and very well too. I regularly clean my grill and replace my drip pans, I keep my pellets store in a dry shed, I cover my grill after every cook, all to protect its longevity…. But this hasn’t proven to help much. 

First is my biggest complaint. Today, for the 4th time my grill has started smoking up in the pellet box, not the grill. I had plenty of pellets, and went outside to check the box multiple times- even making sure they were feeding correctly (because I’ve had this issue before a few times) but when set at 250 after not checking on it for about 30 mins I went out to see my grill at 341 degrees and the pellet box smoking like crazy, while my pork was cool enough to handle. I’ve had this before a few times but today has happened 3 times!! After each time I shut it down, put the meat in the oven, let the grill cool off for an hour at least, put it back on and after about an hour it starts messing up again. Very frustrating.

Second- my grill paint is bubbling/chipping. I’ve seen many other reviews on this. I’ve never had a grease fire, nor have I used max heat other than a handful of times… and I keep my grill covered when not in use, so that’s clearly an issue.

Lastly- just to paint a picture about my current frustrations with the Traeger brand… about 1/3 of my pellet bag is bad. I keep my bags off the floor in my shed and this was a brand new unopened bag that was bad… this is the second time I’ve gotten a bag with bad chips… the last time wasn’t quite as much though- this being a third of my bag at least though proved a much bigger annoyance. 

I have many friends with Traegers with positive experiences, unfortunately mine isn’t great. Just beware I guess… inspect your bags to the best extent and be careful to watch your pellet box. Definitely don’t want that thing catching mid cook. I’ve attached a few pictures, unfortunately didn’t think to snag a pic of the box smoking.

title: No, no, and no. Stay away!!!
text:
I’ve had this grill now for about 3 months and have only used it twice so far. The setup of the grill is pretty self explanatory with the direction guidebook and definitely beneficial to have a couple extra hands to help out to streamline the process. Setting up the wi-fire app was a total breeze as well. Before starting your first cook on the grill, they advise you to ‘season’ the smoker and the directions are provided as well.

Anyway, moving onto the cooking. Relatively a good smoker. My first time smoking, I would say the internal temperature inside the grill remained roughly 10-15 degrees higher or lower at times based on the temperature that I set. Apparently this is pretty standard. It wasn’t until my second time when I noticed that the internal temperature was extremely off. I would set my smoker on the low setting of 180 degrees, and the internal temperature would be sticking around 200-250 degrees!!! I had to ultimately set the grill on it’s lowest temp of 165 degrees for the smoker to continuously stay around the 200-230 area. I called Traeger and they believe its due to the thermocouple… so they sent me a new replacement. What the heck?! After the second cook and I’m already having to replace something? Also, the inside of my smoker has PAINT CHIPPING. I also notified Traeger about this and they believe that there was a fire inside of the smoker which had caused this to happen. They claim that this is not “common” but they can’t do anything about it. What an absolute joke! I paid $1,000+ and I’m stuck with a grill that had paint chipping inside and a messed up thermocouple after two times of usage!!!! What the heck. I do not recommend this grill to anyone.

title: Temperature Issues. Purchaser beware
text:
This grill was gifted for our wedding.. I was very excited to begin using it. The app is very  intuitive and easy to use, it was easy to assemble.  

What I've noticed, my first few cooks I've had significant trouble getting the meat up to to temp in the specified time. For example, 3,2,1 Ribs, after 6 hours were only at 140F (cooking at 220) Condering Traegers recipe tells you to hit 190 or 200F,  I resorted to finishing on the bbq so my guest could eat at a decent time. Embarrassing. 

  At first I thought it was the meat probe, so I checked with another probe and calibrated it, it was fine.   I read everything on the Traeger troubleshooting, used quality pellets, checked for air flow and gaps or anything blocking the heat etc.

What  I found is the cooking surface was significantly lower in temperature then what the digital controller was reading.  170F when the grill said 220. No wonder my food did not cook.

I got ahold of multiple people on the support line, which is handy as its basically text messaging, however there only check for the thermocouple is that is can read the ambient temperature fine and they send you an article about how third party thermometers shouldn't be used because "They cannot detect variance and hot and cold spots".   Well the cold spot is where the meat is cooked, so thats a problem lol.

 That's nonsense. The thermocouple on the grill is placed directly above the flame and fan so the heat  reading is off.   They told me its fine and basically to do better.   It was even suggested that the grill was sitting in the sun which compromised the accuracy lol, I live in southern Canada and its nearly winter. 

 If you research even a little bit online  you can see this is an ongoing issue with the grill Traeger obviously does not take seriously.  Not one that can't be overcome, but do not expect Traeger to take accountability. 

 I will be using my own oven thermometer  to monitor temperature moving forward and will update this review with my findings. I'm excited to use this grill again but cooking my own way, because even at low temperature the food has been great, so when cooked correctly I think it will be even better. 

If I had paid for this grill I would of returned it and purchased something less expensive that I knew I'd have to monitor myself.  At the very least, the meat probe is bang on, maybe I had too high of expectations for the digital controller.

This grill has ruined many special events for me and has destroyed a massive amount of fine meats that I have put a lot of effort and hard work into. I am deeply unsatisfied with this Traeger. title: It's a Good Smoker But Struggles at High Temps
text:
I've had a mixed experience with my Traeger over the last year and a half. When using it at low to mid temperatures, I've been able to achieve a nice bark and smoke flavor on my pork and brisket, and the ease of use is a plus.

However, I wouldn't say that the Traeger is a jack-of-all-trades grill like it's advertised. While it can reach temperatures up to 500 degrees, it requires meticulous cleaning beforehand to avoid grease fire, which can melt the powder coat off of the grill. Additionally, the amount of pellets and time it takes to reach high temperatures is not very efficient.

In my experience, the Traeger is best used as a smoker rather than an all-purpose grill. All of the people I know who own a Traeger also own another grill, including myself. 

One issue that I've encountered is the quality of the powder coat. After experiencing a grease fire because I missed one spot in the grill when cleaning, the coat bubbled and flaked off, which is unacceptable. I'm not the only one in my Traeger circle who has experienced this issue, so it's something to keep in mind.

title: General pros and cons
text:
I've had my 780 grill for about 10 months and use it a minimum of 3 times per week. Previously I had a Traeger Bronson for 5 years and wanted to upgrade. I have to admit the 780 is bigger than I need, and at that time I should have purchased the 575, but here are my findings after cooking on the 780 over 120 times so far. 
The right side and across the front area of the grill are every large areas of cold spots. The biscuit test proved to me that these areas are not prime for maintaining high enough temps. I don't know if the firepot is just not adequate enough to heat the entire area or what might be the answer. Maybe relocating the firepot closer to the right side so that heat spreads across the grill better, to the chimney on the left?
I don't use the wifi option so I can't comment on that. It's just not an important upgrade for me. 
I believe it's because of the large interior space, but none-the-less I've had to increase the temp by anywhere from 25-50 degrees and/or increase the cook times in order to get the same results for many of my routine recipes.
The firepot itself collects ash more readily than my previous Traeger, instead of blowing  the ash into the cavity below the drip tray, causing me to vacuum it out far more often, and causing the grill to heat more slowly, when the firepot is so full of ash, after only short a short time prior to the previous vacuuming.
Because of the large amount of air cavity, it uses far more pellets than my previous Traeger in order to keep that much area at, or close to, the set temp, even though I have an insulation blanket on it year round.
Where the grease flows down into the trough is a much bigger pain in the neck to clean out than the Gen 1 Traegers.
Although it's not a big deal, I'm not a fan of the on/off switch, then setting the temp, plus then pushing the ignite button. The gen 1 Traeger's are easier and faster to start than the Gen 2, in my opinion.
All that said, I'm going to purchase a Pro 22 in the Spring when they run their first seasonal sale, that way the savings will pay for a front tray and part of the cost of a cover. I'll also purchase an insulation blanket because I grill a lot during the cold months and it's a great addition for Winter cooking. 
I'm going back to a smaller grill, because it suits my needs better, and I'm going back to a Gen 1 grill because I like to controller system better for me personally.
Some of my findings are strictly personal, and may be no problem for others, but it never hurts for a company like Traeger to get constructive feedback, no matter what it might be.
I would not buy another brand of pellet grill because I truly feel Traeger is a quality company that produces some great quality items. I hope my comments help some of you who are on the fence and are also helpful to Traeger.

title: Disappointed
text: I have an earlier version of this grill that doesn’t have wheels on two of the legs by the handle.  It has all the Wi-Fi features that this one has though and looks identical otherwise.  I bought this one because our old We’ll loved Traeger got knocked over and damaged.  The new one was purchased in 2019 from Home Depot and I still have it and use it only occasionally now.  There are two issues that make this grill not as good as our old one that got damaged.  That old grill made absolutely the best grilled chicken on the planet.  When the fat from the chicken dripped off on to the foil lined drip pan, it would bathe the chicken in wet steam when it it hit the drip pan which keeps the chicken moist and crisps up the skin perfectly.  As this occurred, more smoke would develop and exhaust out of the chimney.  The issue with this one is that the overwhelmingly vast majority of smoke always comes out of the outlet where the grease trap is.  The chimney has virtually no smoke when it operates which is completely different from our older one!  I called Traeger to discuss this issue and was actually told it wasn’t a problem!  The chicken on the new one is nowhere near as good as the old one and imparts little to no smoke flavor.  In addition, the drip bucket doesn’t catch near the same amount of grease as our old one.  In fact, I have only had to empty the drip bucket once since I’ve had it and I have no idea why it is so radically different than the old one.  The second problem is that the old drip pan showed virtually no signs of rusting over a lot of years of use while the new one shows tons of rust every time I change the foil out that protects the pan.    Both were always kept in my garage and only rolled out when I wanted to use it.  Overall, the new one doesn’t perform nearly as well as the old one.  And with all Traegers, they never get hot enough to produce a decent sear even though the temperature read out says it gets to 500.  Simply put, the one I have won’t hardly sear anything and I’m very disappointed because my older one produced way better cooking results.

title: Design Flaw In My Opinion
text:
I do love using my Traeger grill and I love the food it produces, however, there is a design flaw in my opinion.  

You've designed this great (and somewhat expensive) grill but the grease catcher is basically a bucket that just dangles.  If you cover your grill like I do, it makes it virtually impossible to take the cover off without 1) having to reach under the cover prior to removing the cover or 2) if you forget to do so, having that bucket fall off onto your deck and spill grease everywhere...every single time.  I guess you could replace the bucket liner after every use, but you can't cover the grill until you are sure that all of the grease is done dripping.  A more secure grease bucket would solve that problem.

If you end up using my idea, feel free to send me a Traeger tee shirt, or better yet, a coupon for my local rental store so I can rent a pressure washer and sander so I can get the grease stains out of my deck.

title: PIECE of CRAP that will not smoke in the summer
text: DON'T BUY.  My grill will not go below 225-230 degrees regardless of the setting.  According to Traeger's troubleshooting guide it states if the ambient temperature is above 85 degrees the grill will not function below 225. In other words, you cannot smoke a brisket in the summer. After reading the MANY reviews this is a recognized problem with these grills. Move it to the shade it states.  Today and most any summer day in Texas it is around 90-100 degrees IN THE SHADE.   During the SUMMER is when you smoke briskets etc.  You cannot smoke a brisket at 225 degrees.  It was represented as a top of the line SMOKER by your dealer and the website.  I regret having purchased this grill as there was no disclaimer about not being able to smoke during the summer which is when you expect to use it.  Customer service wants to simply have you replace parts over and over.   I've replaced 2 previous controllers, two RCP's, cleaned the grill, fire pot, and lowered the smoke stack, and the meat probes read 30 degrees different from each other.  The very first day I used it the auger locked up and stripped the bolt that attaches to the motor.  I have had to do all the warranty work myself as no Traeger dealer will work on it, warranty or otherwise.  I am now realizing it is a DESIGN ISSUE as you sell this as a SMOKER....but it won't smoke during the summer when you need it.  If I had just wanted a GRILL I would have bought a grill which gets much hotter for grilling.  Last week they replaced the RCP.  This week I was assured it was the controller.  I found a new controller locally and bought it and it made no difference as I was hoping to smoke a brisket on the 4th of July.  It is a piece of junk IMHO.  THE PROBLEM is the DESIGN not faulty parts.  It simply will not stay below 225 degrees.  I wish I had my money back.  It will ruin a $60 brisket.  My oven cooks better than this.

title: Traeger 575 Wifi Review
text:
I am redoing my rating of Traeger and my 575. At first I was angry and upset that my grill was not working as I thought it should. Well it turns out the Traeger grills are a totally different animal than any of the others out there. I am referring to BBQ's like wood, charcoal, propane, pellets, I have had them all! They all have their places. Let's start with wood, I love wood the smell, the flavor of wood smoked meat. Dislikes direct flame; which is to hard to keep a constant heat and not burn anything. Wood is also the best for smoking. Charcoal- works well for BBQ, even heat, taste is ok. Not able to smoke with charcoal unless you learn how to.  Propane- YEAH! I don't see the reason for it. If you are going to use gas for cooking why not put it on the stove or oven. I'm not a fan.
Now let's move to pellets- I have never heard of or used one. I was intrigued, it is a grill that uses wood yet there is no open flame. OK! I'll try. 
WOW! Traeger's are a little pricey compared to others out there. Let's see what all the fuss is about and the price.
I purchased  the middle of the road Traeger 575. I thankfully purchased it from our local ACE Hardware. They have almost everything you could want for your grill. I went a little crazy and purchased the cover, cleaner brush, the orange cleaner, liners for the BBQ and the drip can. I also purchased the best pellets so far. I have only tried three different ones. The best so far is the Signature, it goes with everything. 
So what I learned is the Traeger 575 wifi is a great grill! I would love to have purchased the Flagship but honestly it is way more grill than I would have ever used. There are a lot of great recipes on the app. The timer and meat thermometer work excellent. The temp of the 575 if cooking small items, like a couple of burgers, a steak and two potatoes', the temp is off a little. Now if you are using it full the temp is dead on. 
Now the grill and the directions tell you to clean your grill after every two to three uses or depending on how greasy the meal is. MAKE SURE TO CLEAN your grill. A quick vacuum and wipedown is all it takes. Make sure to use the tray liners, makes cleaning easy.
Now for the cooking. I got mine back in July and I have cooked everything I can at this grill. I have to say it is AWESOME! I cooked "bacon" Yes! bacon right on the grill. The bacon stayed the same shape as I put it on the grill and came out perfectly crispy. In fact it was so perfect, my wife thought it was fake. 
Everything and I mean everything came out wonderful. 
The strange thing to me is when your grill heats up and tells you it is ready, you open the lid and expect to have this huge wave if heat hit you in the face. It never does. As well as when you place your food on the grill, you expect to get burnt by the flame. There isn't one!
If you have never cooked with one you need to find someone with a Traeger and become friends. LOL!
Maybe you can go down to your local retailer that sells them and ask them to have a Traeger demo day! Here you go Traeger have someone who is familiar with cooking on a Traeger and have demo days on a weekend. Cook and have food for people to sample.
P.S. for smoking I have done a few things that help with more smoke. I adjusted the top hat down a little bit and turned the temp down. I get more smoke this way.
I do not work for Traeger nor are they paying, giving or promising me anything. I just really like my grill. Now I want the Flagship just to see what it is capable of. I also love to BBQ, so I am a little biased. I would rather be cooking outside than inside.

title: This review is for unboxing and setup review only
text:
Delivered 30 November 2023. Today is 06 January 2024. 

The unboxing and assembly instructions were very easy to follow and were spot-on.  Unfortunately, the chimney cap bolt was improperly machined (i.e., the bolt threads were not properly machined to match the threads of the pipe) which caused the chimney cap bolt to become cross-threaded as I was installing the bolt into the pipe.  The threads on the chimney pipe were undamaged.  I purchased an after-market chimney cap and chimney pipe, they were not sold separately, and I only used the nuts and bolts from the new cap to secure the original chimney cap to the original chimney pipe.  The after-market nuts and bolts were a perfect match for the original chimney cap and chimney pipe.

As of this review, 06 January 2024, I have not used the Traeger for grilling because I wanted to resolve the cross-threaded bolt issue.

title: Poor lid construction
text: I purchased my Pro 780 at the Houston Rodeo several years ago. I can say I enjoy it but it is a shame to me that it does not completely meet this statement found on their website:  "WILL THIS GRILL FALL APART WITHIN A YEAR? Traeger grills are built-to-last. Every Traeger features superior structural construction, an ultra-sturdy base, and built-tough steel legs. If something does go wrong, our ironclad 3-year warranty and 365 days of customer service will cover any issue that may arise." Honestly the only place it has superior struction is in the base of the pit but not where the pit is used the most which is the lid. Less than a year the the opening and closing of the lid weakened the lid hinges and screws. The hinges began to bend then tear due to not being able to handle the weight of the lid when opened. There is nothing off load the lid's wiehgt off the hinges. I looked at other pellet grills such as the Ptit Boss and saw how they structured their support for the lid when open. I wish Treagar had the same. Due to the hinges bending the door does not close correctly. I did call customer service. I had to go through a process I am sure they have done quite often with may other customers and of course it did not resolve the issue. They sent another lid, hinges and handle but in no time the same thing is happening. The hinges are bending due to the weight of the lid and lid not closing correctly. I guess I will have to call agian to get it all replaced. These pits are not cheap but it sould not be advertised as "superior structural construction" because the lid system is not superior at all.

title: Not much smoke flavor!
text: Pro 575 maintains heat well. I haven't seen a big difference between my meater thermometer and the on board sensor.  Others have reported a large discrepancy but I didn't experience that. It disappointing that this model doesn't have a super smoke mode.  Even keeping temp below 225F doesn't provide the same flavor as the super smoke mode.  I've had to put a separate smoke canister inside. It's a pain but necessary to get flavor.  The hook the grease pail hangs on is poorly designed.  If you use a cover, the pail  falls when you remove the cover. I needed to design a latch that retains the pail. It could been designed a lot better without adding cost.  Hopper clean out is difficult as the door is behind the grill and the pellets do not free flow out of the hopper. A stick needs to be poked through the anger protection screen.  I'm sure that many people have just removed the screen.  The controller is easy to operate and the Mobil app screen is laid out well.  Cleaning the ash put requires all the heat shields and grates to be removed. Chamber cannot be removed and dumped, it has to be vacuumed.  Other competing grill have buckets that can be removed.  All in all, heat stability is good, controller is good but the pellet unloading process and ash pit cleaning ergonomics could be a lot better.  It a middle of the rode product at best.

title: A really nice upgrade to an older version Traeger.
text:
I bought the Pro 780 to replace my Big Texas that was about 15 years old after it finally failed.  I got it and the full-length cover at Ace Hardware in early December 2024.  I did have to get a neighbor to help me get it out of the back of my truck gently - it weighs 187 pounds, so keep that in mind if you get one yourself.  I'd recommend a hand truck to move it to where you're going to build it.  

The packaging that was used was incredibly well done and would make it fairly difficult, but not impossible, to damage in transit.  The only drawback to that was that there was a literal mountain of cardboard that needed to be dealt with, but no regrets...

The assembly was very straightforward - the parts were all labeled, and the directions were very clear.  Tools need for assembly were all included, and I used them, even though I have better, to assemble it - they worked just fine.  They recommend having two people to assemble, but if you take your time, it's one-person job.  I recommend using the largest pieces of cardboard as an assembly service so the grill body can be moved around without scratching it.  The WiFire set up was pretty easy as well with the app.

It was a pretty easy job to get it built and "burned in" in a single afternoon.  I did baby back ribs as the first cook, and they came out excellent.

One suggestion for Trager - Please additional probe ports - one is just inadequate.  Two would be better, but four would be awesome!

I heard great reviews about these Traeger grills and thought well they’re on sale so I caught it on sale ordered at the Ace Hardware store in Dyer Indiana and I am so disappointed! When you cook ribs with a Traeger grill, you might as well cook them in your  oven. I used their famous three to one recipe took an extra two hours to cook because it was cold out and the grill is not insulated so it was too cold (25deg no wind). When we ate the ribs, there was zero smoke flavor whatsoever so I could’ve cooked them in my stove and Saved $20.00 in wood pellets. After all, they don’t tell you this, but the Traeger grill doesn’t emit smoke after about 180° but the recipe for ribs starts at 220deg so you’ve got zero smoke cooked  in them so put the ribs in your oven save $18 bucks or $20 bucks in traeger pellets. The kicker is I tried the grill two times thinking well. Maybe it was a fluke the first time it didn’t cook for crap cooked the second time with a grill recipe thinking maybe that’ll work and it’s still sucked. Tried to return the grill, but no once you’ve used the grill, you cannot return it so please be aware. I’m so disappointed.

I’m stuck now. After buying grill, pellets, cover, etc I’m $750 into a piece of crap. 

Don’t DO IT, I hope I can help someone or 2 from not getting ripped off.

title: Terrible probes and temp management.
text: 2 stars because ease of use. Doesnt hold temp well. Constant 10 plus degree swings up and down. The super smoke function hasn't functioned out of the box. Not that it really does much. Build quality is good actually assembly a breeze. I like many things about it. title: TLDR, WIFIRE WILL NOT CONNECT DONT WAIST YOUR TIME
text: DO NOT BUY THIS GRILL!!! I never post reviews good or bad, but i felt it was important to warn potential buyers. This grill will not connect to wifi. I’ve spent hours with customer support just for them to tell me that it’s a known issue with the app and there is NO ETA of a fix or an explanation. They basically said “works for some and not for others” with no clear answer of what device will connect. I’ve tried 5 different devices now, IOS, android and google and none have been able to connect to wifire. Can buy the same size Traeger without the “fancy” wifire for almost $400 less and save your self time and energy trying to connect the thing to wifi. I was even willing to buy a new controller, but support said that wasn’t the issue and would not fix the concern.

title: Hasn't let me down yet
text: Bought this a couple of days before Thanksgiving with the goal of trying to cook my first turkey for my family. I owned a Pit Boss before I purchased for a couple of years amd it was an absolute headache every time I used it. The Trager on the other hand has been a dream. I used Meat Church YouTube video for spatchcock turkey with their Hickory rub and I will never let anyone ever cook a turkey for me again. I used to hate turkey to be honest, and now I love it if I'm the one cooking. I have done multiple sets of ribs which are always successful, and recently I did my first brisket and pork butt which were overnight cooks. Traeger hasn't disconnected or stopped cooking yet. Everything I've tried on it is successful. Can't say that for their competitors. Think my wife is going to get me the Pimpmygrill rack system for father's day and I'll officially be unstoppable. Tip for new users, use Knottywood or Lumberjack pellets if you really want to lay the smoke on good. Thanks for providing such a consistent and awesome product Traeger.

title: Unfortunate avoidable design shortfalls.
text:
LOVED this grill when I first got it a couple of years ago.  Still love the flavor of the food (when you use quality pellets), but there are some disappointing shortfalls.  

1)  I couldn't believe a $1,000 grill wouldn't come with a shelf already.  Had to purchase on separately for $80. 

2)  The lid is thin and, for some inexplicable reason, Traeger didn't see fit to reinforce where the lid restrictor is attached to the lid and the grill, inevitability leading to the lid bending enough over time that you don't get a tight fit when the lid's closed.

3) Seems like other manufacturers figured out that it's a good idea to sell heat resistant gaskets and lid locking devices to rectify this.  Although I was able to purchase an Oklahoma Joe's brand gasket at Lowe's, the lid still is not tight.  Oklahoma Joe's, LavaLock and others sell a lid latch kit for smokers, but, unfortunately, they don't seem to be compatible with he Traeger Pro 780 due too the narrow distance on the sides of the lid.

What i thought was a great pellet grill when I purchased it, turned out to be an overpriced average one.  Will definitely consider another brand when I upgrade.

title: No longer a Traeger customer after this
text:
Meat on one side of the grill is raw, and meet on the other side is burnt. Went through all the troubleshooting with Traeger. They sent a few parts to try replacing and it did not fix the issue. This is my second Traeger. I know how they are supposed to work. The company refuses to do a warranty replacement as they say, “after reviewing the case based on the data we have about the behaviour of your grill we came to the conclusion it his working as designed.” They offered me a 25% discount on a grill of a model of their choosing. 

I have to say that I am extremely disappointed with Traeger's decision. While they have concluded that my grill is "working as designed," the reality is that it is not performing as a grill should. It consistently fails to meet reasonable expectations, and I have spent a significant amount of time trying to troubleshoot an issue that clearly impacts its performance.

Offering me a 25% discount on the purchase of another Traeger is not an acceptable resolution. After this experience, I have no confidence in purchasing another one of their products.

What is most disappointing is that Traeger has chosen not to stand behind its product. I purchased this grill because of the company's reputation for quality and customer service, and this experience has completely changed my opinion of the brand.

I have recommended Traeger to many people over the years, but I will no longer be doing so. In fact, I don't even feel comfortable selling my current grill second-hand because I don't believe it performs as it should, and I wouldn't feel right passing that problem on to someone else.

This outcome has left me incredibly disappointed and disheartened. As a result, I no longer consider myself a Traeger customer, and I have no intention of purchasing another Traeger product in the future.

I had hoped for a resolution that reflected confidence in your products and commitment to your customers. Unfortunately, this decision has accomplished the opposite.
